info.title: Orbit API
info.description:
Public API for Orbit by YunZheng LAB (AS204921): authoritative DNS, Shield CDN, security rules, hosted RPKI and compute.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer orb_…` (create tokens in the console under **API tokens**; API access must be enabled on your account).
Errors are always `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`. Tokens are limited to 300 requests per minute (`X-RateLimit-*` headers).
Every response carries `X-Orbit-Api-Version: 1`. The legacy `/api/*` RPC endpoints remain for the console and are deprecated for integrations.

max_video.description: how many participants may publish a camera at once

public_join.description: whether the room answers on rtc.yunzheng.space. Off means the room is API-only and a leaked room key grants nothing.

require_verify.description: require an Orbit Verify token before a join token is issued

verify_level.description: the security level that check runs at

has_passcode.description: whether a passcode is set. The passcode itself is stored as an HMAC and is never returned.

join_url.description: the link a participant opens; null when link access is off

live.description: participants the nodes are currently reporting

preferred_city.description: the city you asked for; a preference, not a pin

city.description: where the room actually is; null until the first join, and not always the one asked for — a full city is fallen back from rather than refused

record.description: whether calls in this room are recorded, one file per participant. Requires the rtc_record pack feature to turn on; always safe to turn off.

last_error.description: why the platform itself last changed something about this room — today only the monthly recording storage ceiling does that

system.description: which product made this room on your behalf, or null for one you created. `?all=1` is what lists them.

cascade.description: nearest-location routing: each participant connects to the Orbit location nearest them, and the locations in one call are linked automatically. Off, everyone in the room connects to the one location in `city`.

max_video.description: 0 means the room carries voice only

city.description: which city to run in. A preference: if it is full when the first person arrives, another city takes the room. Omit to let the platform choose.

cascade.description: nearest-location routing — each participant connects to the location nearest them, and the locations in one call are linked automatically. On by default for new rooms; rooms created before it existed are off until you turn it on. A change applies to the next person who joins.

record.description: PATCH only. Record calls in this room: one file per participant plus a manifest, kept in Orbit's object storage and metered as rtc_rec_gb. Turning it on requires the rtc_record pack feature; turning it off never does.

passcode.description: PATCH only, write-only. Omit to leave unchanged; send an empty string to remove.

rec_id.description: public and unguessable — the address IS the capability

ended_at.description: set once the node's manifest has landed

replay_url.description: the manifest (index.json): who was in the call, and which file each of them is

tracks.description: one entry per participant, in join order

peer_id.description: the participant id the join token carried — your own user id when the token came from your backend

video.description: the video MIME type this participant published, empty when they published none

start_ms.description: offset from the start of the call at which this participant joined

url.description: the file itself, at the same unguessable address as the manifest

label.description: a display name for this participant

peer_id.description: your own identifier for this person, 8–40 of A–Z a–z 0–9 _ -. Stable across sessions is what makes a participant list and moderation mean anything. Omit it and one is generated for this join only.

near.description: where this participant is, for a room with `cascade` on: the location they are sent to is the one nearest this point. Your server's own location says nothing about the person's, so pass theirs — coordinates, or just a country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Omit it and they join the room's first location. A value that cannot be read is ignored rather than refused.

readonly.description: mint an observer seat: it receives every track in the room and publishes none. The restriction is inside the signed token, so it holds at the media node rather than in your page — an observer whose offer asks to send is refused `read-only`, and an observer is left out of the participant list the others are shown. Only this endpoint can mint one; the public join path never does, because who may only watch is your application's decision about a person it has identified, not a stranger's about themselves.

media_host.description: the ONE machine this participant sends media to — not an anycast address. In a room with `cascade` on, the location nearest this participant.

token.description: hand this to the media host; valid for two minutes

perm.description: what the token above was signed to permit — `rw` publishes and receives, `ro` only receives. A report of what was signed, never an input: this field is read from the token, and changing it changes nothing.

ice_servers.description: hand this to RTCPeerConnection unchanged. It is usually empty — almost every call reaches the media host directly, and the relay is only offered to the cities that run one. When it is not empty it names ONE relay under two transports (TLS on 443, plain UDP on 3478) with a credential minted for this seat: it expires, and it can relay to this node's own media address and nowhere else.

SiteThreats.description: Threat intelligence for one Shield site: how much of its traffic came from subjects the platform considers risky. Aggregates only — never individual visitors.

sampled.description: Always true: derived from the sampled request logs (every security event, pass-through capped per minute)

risky_subjects.description: Subjects in the high or critical band

bands.description: Share of sampled requests per risk band (low < 30 ≤ medium < 60 ≤ high < 85 ≤ critical)

top_fingerprints.description: Client software by its protocol fingerprints (TLS JA4 and HTTP/2), most requests first. Aggregates only: a fingerprint describes the software, never the visitor, and is never reported beside an address.

score.description: Platform score of this fingerprint, or null if it has none yet

tags.description: Why subjects were considered risky

timeline.description: One point per bucket, oldest first, zero-filled

visibility.description: There is no public directory, so both are reachable only by address. 'unlisted' means the address cannot be guessed; it is not access control.

state.description: whether a broadcaster is connected. It is NOT the whole answer to 'is anything playing' — see `on`.

on.description: what viewers get right now: 'live' is somebody broadcasting, 'programme' is the channel playing its own running order because nobody is, 'off' is nothing. A programme is delivered exactly like a broadcast — one timeline, everybody at the same point.

placement.description: how the channel is reached. 'city' is that one city's own address, over its own transit; 'anycast' is one address for the whole network, reached through ours from wherever the viewer is. Both are cached at the edge, so this changes the path, not the number of origin pulls.

renditions.description: how many qualities are offered BELOW the published one. 0 means viewers receive exactly what was published.

quality_note.description: what a viewer will experience, in one sentence

started_at.description: when the current broadcast started; null when offline

ingest_url.description: paste into OBS as the Server field. Always RTMPS — every channel has this address, whatever else it allows.

ingest_url_rtmp.description: the plain RTMP address, present only while allow_rtmp is true and the ingest city opens a plaintext port. Warning: a stream key sent to this address travels unencrypted — it is the publish command's stream name, so anyone on the path sees it every time the encoder connects.

allow_rtmp.description: whether this channel also accepts plain RTMP (see ingest_url_rtmp). Off by default.

latency_mode.description: low: about 3–5 seconds behind with a keyframe every 1–2 seconds; the segment length follows the encoder's keyframe interval, so an encoder sending a keyframe every 8 seconds stays about 15 seconds behind. standard: about 15 seconds behind, and tolerant of any keyframe interval.

delay_s.description: extra seconds the audience is held behind the broadcaster, applied at the origin, so it cannot be skipped by a player.

city.description: where ingest lands. For an anycast channel this is where the LAST broadcast landed, not a promise about the next one.

key_id.description: identifies the current key; never the key itself

record.description: whether broadcasts on this channel are recorded and kept as a replayable VOD. Requires the stream_record pack feature to turn on; always safe to turn off.

watermark.description: where a burned-in copyright mark sits on every viewer's picture: 'off', 'br' (bottom right) or 'tl' (top left). It reads “Orbit Stream” with your UID beneath it, is drawn while the broadcast is encoded rather than by the player, and is therefore in the recording as well. Turning the watermark on re-encodes the top quality instead of passing it through untouched, so the channel uses one more encoder on the ingest node and what viewers receive is no longer byte-for-byte what you published.

watermark_note.description: present only while the watermark is on, saying in one sentence what it costs

realtime_play.description: near-real-time playback over WebRTC beside the HLS delivery. About one second behind, and it is the broadcaster's own picture. It needs the encoder to send no B-frames (in OBS: x264 options bf=0, or the zerolatency tune), or the node re-encodes for this path, which uses one more encoder and is no longer byte for byte what was published. A channel with a watermark is always re-encoded for this path, so the mark is in what realtime viewers see too. Viewers connect to the ingest city directly rather than to an edge, so keep large audiences on the default path.

whep_url.description: the WHEP address a player POSTs an SDP offer to, present only while realtime_play is on. It is the ingest city's own address, because a WebRTC flow has nothing an edge can cache; our player tries it first and falls back to playback_url on its own.

realtime_note.description: present only while realtime_play is on, saying what it is and what it needs

recording_store.description: where this channel's recordings are kept. Everything you sent is echoed back except the secret, which is write-only.

kind.description: 'ours' keeps recordings in our storage and meters them as storage-months. 'byo' writes them into a bucket of yours over the S3 API — R2, OSS, S3 or anything else that speaks it — and is NOT charged storage-months, because we hold nothing. Transfer through us is metered as stream_gb either way.

endpoint.description: scheme and host of the bucket service. No bucket name, no path.

region.description: 'auto' for R2; the bucket's own region for AWS and Aliyun. It is part of the signature, so it has to be right.

prefix.description: optional folder inside the bucket; every object this channel writes lands under it.

secret.description: sent when setting or changing the credential, never returned. Stored encrypted under a Worker secret and decrypted only for the length of one write. Omit it to keep the secret already stored.

secret_set.description: whether a secret is stored. The secret itself is never shown again.

enabled.description: whether the channel plays this when nobody is publishing to it. A broadcaster always pre-empts it, and it comes back after they leave.

mode.description: 'loop' plays the items in order, forever. 'relay' re-serves one live source under this channel's own address and takes exactly one item.

items.description: The running order, in the order given, at most 50. PUT replaces the whole list — that is how you reorder and how you remove.

kind.description: 'recording' is one of this account's own finished recordings; 'url' is an https address of an MP4 or an HLS playlist; 'channel' is another of this account's channels, relayed.

ref.description: for 'recording', the orc_… id — it must be finished, not deleted, owned by this account and kept in our storage (a recording in your own bucket is replayed from a signed address that expires, so it cannot be put in a programme). For 'url', an https address; plain http is refused. For 'channel', the other channel's ops_… playback id; in this phase it must belong to the same account, because relaying somebody else's channel needs their permission and there is nowhere yet to give it.

title.description: what to call this item in the console. Never shown to viewers.

exported.description: objects moved out of our storage into your bucket by this call

held_objects.description: objects still held here afterwards; 0 means the recording is entirely in your bucket

placement.description: 'city' publishes to one city's own address. 'anycast' publishes to one global address that always reaches the nearest city with room — a pack feature, and not combinable with `city`.

city.description: ingest city, for placement 'city'; omit to take whichever has room

renditions.description: how many lower qualities to produce (1080p, 720p, 480p, 360p, highest first, never above what was published). Defaults to what the packs allow; a number above that is refused rather than capped.

record.description: record broadcasts on this channel (PATCH only; a pack feature to turn on).

latency_mode.description: PATCH only. low: about 3–5 seconds behind with a keyframe every 1–2 seconds; the segment length follows the encoder's keyframe interval, so an encoder sending a keyframe every 8 seconds stays about 15 seconds behind. standard: about 15 seconds behind. Takes effect on the next broadcast.

delay_s.description: PATCH only. Extra seconds the audience is held behind the broadcaster, applied at the origin, so it cannot be skipped by a player. Takes effect on the next broadcast.

watermark.description: PATCH only. Burn a copyright mark into every viewer's picture: 'off', 'br' (bottom right) or 'tl' (top left). Turning the watermark on re-encodes the top quality instead of passing it through untouched, so the channel uses one more encoder on the ingest node and what viewers receive is no longer byte-for-byte what you published. Takes effect on the next broadcast.

allow_rtmp.description: PATCH only. Also accept plain RTMP on this channel, for encoders that cannot do TLS. Warning: a stream key sent over plain RTMP travels unencrypted, because the key is the publish command's stream name. Takes effect on the next broadcast; the RTMPS address keeps working either way.

realtime_play.description: PATCH only. Offer near-real-time playback over WebRTC beside the HLS delivery, at whep_url. About one second behind, and it is the broadcaster's own picture. It needs the encoder to send no B-frames (in OBS: x264 options bf=0, or the zerolatency tune), or the node re-encodes for this path, which uses one more encoder and is no longer byte for byte what was published. A channel with a watermark is always re-encoded for this path, so the mark is in what realtime viewers see too. Viewers connect to the ingest city directly rather than to an edge, so keep large audiences on the default path. A viewer who joins between keyframes waits up to one keyframe interval for a picture. Takes effect on the next broadcast; HLS keeps working either way.

recording_store.description: PATCH only. Send { kind: 'byo', endpoint, region, bucket, prefix, access_key, secret } to keep this channel's recordings in your own bucket, or { kind: 'ours' } to bring them back to ours (which forgets the credentials). Saving PROVES the bucket works: we write a test object under the prefix, read it back and delete it, and refuse the setting in one sentence if any of that fails.

stream_key.description: shown once, at creation. It cannot be recovered; rotate to get a new one

note.description: when the key starts being accepted

revoke_now.description: also end the broadcast on air. Without it the broadcast continues on the old key until it ends

note.description: when the new key starts being accepted

bytes_out.description: what left the ingest node: segments pulled by the edges, plus anything sent straight to near-real-time viewers

plain.description: whether this broadcast was published over plain RTMP rather than RTMPS, i.e. whether its stream key was sent unencrypted. Recorded per broadcast and not changed by turning the channel's switch off afterwards.

programme.description: whether this session was the channel playing its own programme rather than somebody broadcasting to it. Its bytes_out is metered as transfer; it has no bytes_in and counts no ingest-minutes.

realtime_encode.description: whether the node had to re-encode the picture for the near-real-time path during this broadcast, because the encoder sent B-frames. A broadcast whose encoder sent none is forwarded untouched and costs no encoder.

realtime_viewers.description: the largest number of near-real-time viewers this broadcast carried at once. Their traffic is in bytes_out with everything else.

ingest_behind_ms.description: the furthest the media we received ever fell behind the wall clock during this broadcast, in milliseconds. It grows when the publisher's uplink or a relay in front of us buffers and sends late, so the fix is a lower bitrate or a better network at that end.

encode_behind_ms.description: the furthest the media we had written ever fell behind the media we had received, in milliseconds. It grows when the ingest node cannot encode this channel in real time, and it sits at up to one segment length even on a healthy broadcast because the segment being written is not in the playlist yet.

stall_ms.description: the longest the ingest node's writes into its encoder blocked for in any twenty-second interval of this broadcast, in milliseconds. When this is more than a few hundred, the node was slowing the publisher down and the publisher's encoder will have reported dropped frames; the fix is fewer qualities, the watermark off, or a lower frame rate on this channel.

direct.description: whether this city has an address of its own that viewers connect to directly. Without one its channels are still delivered, on the address the whole network shares.

rec_id.description: public and unguessable — the address IS the capability. A private recording is only ever reached through it.

ended_at.description: set once the broadcast's final segment has been folded into the VOD playlist

store.description: which bucket this recording's objects are in — the channel's setting at the time it was recorded, not now.

held_objects.description: objects of this recording sitting in OUR storage because your bucket refused them. 0 is the ordinary case; anything else is what a re-export moves.

replay_url.description: a VOD HLS playlist the same player plays. For a 'byo' recording this is a short-lived signed address against your own bucket, minted on each read and never stored; null while the recording is unfinished or partly held here.

replay_note.description: present only when there is no replay address, saying why in one sentence

title.description: what the watch page calls this recording; null falls back to '<channel> · <date>'.

description.description: a sentence or two shown under the title on the watch page.

visibility.description: who may reach the watch page: 'public' is listed in the library and indexable; 'unlisted' is reachable only by its link and listed nowhere; 'private' is the owner (or an admin) only, a 404 to anyone else.

passcode_set.description: whether the watch page asks for a passcode first. The passcode itself is never returned; send passcode:'' in an update to clear it.

published_at.description: when this recording first became public; null until it has been. The library orders by it.

views.description: a coarse, deduped count of watch-page hits — one per viewer per minute, never a per-viewer history.

watch_url.description: the shareable watch page. Omitted for a private recording you do not own.

channel.description: the channel's name (on a single-recording GET only).

playback_id.description: the channel's public id (on a single-recording GET only, for the owner or an admin).

title.description: what to call this recording on its watch page. Null or omitted leaves it as the '<channel> · <date>' default.

description.description: a sentence or two under the title. Null clears it.

visibility.description: 'public' lists it in the library and lets it be indexed; 'unlisted' keeps it reachable only by its link; 'private' restricts it to you (or an admin). The first time you make a recording public it takes a publication date the library orders by.

passcode.description: set to require a passcode on the watch page (stored only as a hash, never returned); send an empty string to clear it. A wrong passcode is throttled.

key.description: the capability. Whoever holds it may ask to join; the passcode and human verification are what decide whether they may.

kind.description: 'room' keeps history for `retention_days`. 'live' keeps the last few hundred messages in memory and nothing on disk — it is what a broadcast's chat is.

city.description: where this conversation lives. Its history lives there too, so it does not move.

peers.description: people connected, as of the last report

messages.description: messages this conversation has ever carried

retention_days.description: 0 for a live room, whose history is never written down

public_join.description: false means this conversation answers nothing on the public join path, and a leaked key buys an attacker nothing

join_url.description: the hosted page, when public join is on

system.description: Which product made this conversation on your behalf, or null for one you created. `?all=1` is what lists them.

city.description: where it lives. A pack feature; omit it and the city with the most room takes it.

max_peers.description: people at once, up to what the packs allow and never above 20000

passcode.description: an empty value clears it. What is stored is an HMAC; there is nothing to read back.

label.description: the display name this participant appears under

peer_id.description: your own identifier for them; one is generated when omitted

readonly.description: mint a seat that reads the conversation and cannot write to it. The restriction is inside the signed token, so it holds at the node rather than in your page: a read-only seat that sends is answered `read-only` and stays connected, still receiving. Only this endpoint can mint one — the public join path never does, because who may only read is your application's decision about a person it has identified, not a stranger's about themselves.

perm.description: what the token you were just handed permits. `ro` is a seat that reads and cannot write. This is a report of what was signed — the node reads the token, never this field.

TalkHistory.description: A page of a conversation, read from the machine that holds it. Messages are never copied into the control plane, and every read of one is recorded in your account's audit log.

room.description: the conversation this page came from

from.description: the cursor this page was read from

next.description: the cursor for the next page, or null when this is everything the node holds. A short page is proof there is no more, so it never carries one.

note.description: present only when there was something to say about an otherwise ordinary answer — a live chat, which writes no history down, answers with an empty page and this sentence.

seq.description: the conversation's own number for this message, ascending and never reused

id.description: the sender's idempotency key — a resend after a reset carries the same one and is answered with the seq the first copy already has

peer.description: who sent it. Through the backend door this is your own user id; through the public one it is a guest's seat and means nothing outside the conversation.

label.description: the display name they appeared under

asset_id.description: 22 random characters. For an unlisted video the address IS the access control.

ladder.description: the qualities this video carries, tallest first

playback_url.description: the master playlist. null for a private video — ask POST /vod/assets/{id}/playback for a signed one, and for one that is not ready yet.

progress.description: how far the transcode has got, while it is running

stage.description: what the node is doing right now: download, probe, encode <height>, upload, poster

size.description: the file's exact size in bytes. Required: the part count and the sealed object are both checked against it.

parts.description: how many parts the size you declared may be cut into

playlist.description: the media playlist under the delivery host

expires_in.description: private videos only: how long the signed link lives, in seconds

url.description: the master playlist, signed when the video is private

expires_at.description: null when the link does not expire

key.description: the signing secret (ovp_…). Shown once — store it now. Sign `<asset_id>.<exp>` with HMAC-SHA256 and send it as ?exp=&kid=&sig= (base64url, unpadded).

code.description: The 3-4-3 letter meeting code. Null once it has been recycled — a code returns to circulation thirty days after the meeting ended, and the meeting's own record outlives it.

next_at.description: The next occurrence, computed when the meeting is written so a list can be ordered by it

waiting_room.description: Everybody who is not the host waits until a host lets them in

guests_allowed.description: Whether somebody without a YunZheng account may join with a name

city.description: Which city the meeting's rooms prefer. A preference, not a pin: a full city is fallen back from rather than refused.

passcode.description: Whether a passcode is set. The passcode itself is stored as an HMAC and is never returned.

session_id.description: The session running right now, or null

live.description: Whether a session of it is running right now

seq.description: The state channel's version number. It moves on every state write; a browser polls with ?since= and is answered 304 while it has not.

kind.description: join, knock, admit, deny, mute, remove, lock, share_start, share_stop, record_start, record_stop, leave, start, end, reaction

event.description: The same string as `kind`, under the name every other audit table in the console reads

state.description: recording while the meeting runs, composing while the node makes one picture out of the per-participant files, ready once it is a video

waiting_room.description: Everybody who is not the host waits until a host lets them in

guests_allowed.description: Whether somebody without a YunZheng account may join with a name

city.description: Which city the meeting's rooms prefer. A preference, not a pin: a full city is fallen back from rather than refused.

waiting_room.description: Everybody who is not the host waits until a host lets them in

guests_allowed.description: Whether somebody without a YunZheng account may join with a name

city.description: Which city the meeting's rooms prefer. A preference, not a pin: a full city is fallen back from rather than refused.

ended.description: How many running sessions were stopped

slug.description: A URL-shaped handle, lowercase and hyphenated

owner_email.description: The principal every resource in this organisation actually hangs off

apps.description: Which applications members may open. Absent keys are on.

sub.description: The IdP subject. Null only for a row whose person has never signed in.

sent.description: Whether the invitation mail left the platform. The invitation exists either way.

auto_meet.description: Every finished Meet recording is copied here

node_host.description: the registrar and WebRTC host for this PBX's location

credentials.description: create only: the SIP passwords of the extensions a template made, shown once

intl_prefixes.description: country calling codes international calls may go to; international calling needs at least one

daily_spend_micros.description: platform-line spend per UTC day after which outbound calls pause; 0 = no daily limit

user_email.description: the YunZheng account this extension is assigned to

user_bound.description: whether that person has signed in since it was assigned

password.description: create only: the SIP password, shown once

csv.description: number,name,user_email[,outbound_class[,record]] per line; a header line is skipped

destination.description: ext:<n>, vm:<n>, ivr:<id>, group:<n>, queue:<n>, tc:<id>, conf:<n>, ann:<media id> or hangup

did.description: an E.164 number or a dial pattern; empty with no number_id means every unmatched call

destination.description: ext:<n>, vm:<n>, ivr:<id>, group:<n>, queue:<n>, tc:<id>, conf:<n>, ann:<media id> or hangup

match.description: X=0-9, Z=1-9, N=2-9, [1-5], . one or more, ! zero or more

additionalProperties.description: ext:<n>, vm:<n>, ivr:<id>, group:<n>, queue:<n>, tc:<id>, conf:<n>, ann:<media id> or hangup

invalid.description: ext:<n>, vm:<n>, ivr:<id>, group:<n>, queue:<n>, tc:<id>, conf:<n>, ann:<media id> or hangup

sip_in.description: whether calls from other SIP services are accepted

noanswer.description: vm:<extension>@<pbx id>: the voicemail a call goes to when no endpoint answers; empty = the first endpoint's

owned.description: false for a number that rings an extension assigned to you but belongs to the PBX's owner

endpoints.description: the extensions it rings, all at once

number.description: the Voice number it already rings for

pbx_owned.description: held by the PBX's owner (assigned from the console) rather than by a person

released.description: the number rang nowhere else and was released

plan_label.description: Display name of the plan (e.g. Free)

Quota.description: Limits belong to the account, not to a service. An account may hold several packs and their limits add up; a limit of 0 means unmetered and absorbs every other pack.

label.description: Display name of the merged packs, e.g. "Pro + Zone add-on ×2"

usage.description: Counted across every service the account owns

secret.description: Returned only when the endpoint is created - store it, it is never shown again

events.description: Event names, or ["*"] for all. Defaults to all.

Range.description: A slice of a reverse zone handed to one principal. Reverse DNS is only delegated on /24 (or nibble) boundaries, so a customer's /29 is expressed here rather than as a delegation.

owner.description: Principal: an address, team:<id>, or partner:<slug>:<ref>

addresses.description: How many addresses the range covers (a string: a /64 does not fit in a number)

enabled.description: A suspended grant confers nothing but still occupies its place in the zone

prefix.description: CIDR inside the zone. Host bits are masked off.

owner.description: Principal to grant it to. Must already exist.

external_ref.description: Partner credentials only: the partner's own customer id. The principal is created if needed.

enabled.description: Suspend or resume. A suspended grant keeps its place in the zone so nothing can be granted over it, and confers no access at all. Records are never touched.

RangeGrant.description: The covering reverse zone is found from the prefix, so a billing system does not have to know internal zone ids.

ranges.description: Every range this customer holds, with the record names each covers

names.description: The record names this range lets you edit

enabled.description: A suspended partner keeps read access and loses every write

brand.description: Embedded panel branding: name, logo, accent, support_url

attribution.description: Whether the panel carries the line naming the platform. True unless this partner has a white-label arrangement; if you render your own panel, honour it.

acting_for.description: The customer principal this credential acts as, if any

external_ref.description: Your own customer id. Calling again with the same value returns the same principal.

SiteOrigin.description: Exactly one of these, or none of them to go back to the origin address on the record.

PagesProject.description: A static site. It is served ONLY on a hostname you own — there is no subdomain of ours, by design: user content under our own name would put every service we run behind one browser blocklist entry.

name.description: Slug. Appears in the console and in storage keys; never to a visitor.

live_deploy.description: The deploy being served. Rolling back moves this and nothing else.

PagesDeploy.description: One upload of a whole site. Files go into it one at a time, then it is finished — and a finished deploy is immutable.

LinkTunnel.description: A tunnel from your origin to the edge. Your origin opens no inbound port; it dials out and Shield pulls through the tunnel.

pop2.description: Second landing city, if one is configured

addr4.description: The address Shield reaches this origin at. Internal to the platform.

local_url.description: What the connector forwards to on your own server

last_error.description: What the connector last failed to reach on your server, if anything

sites.description: Shield hostnames served through this tunnel

pop_id2.description: A second landing point. The connector holds both, so one going away is not an outage.

token.description: Shown once. Install it on your origin.

MailDomain.description: A domain we accept mail for — either forwarded (zone_id set) or a BYO mailbox/forward/both domain on your own server (server_id set).

domain.description: Legacy (forwarding) domains only; a BYO domain's name is in `name`.

catch_all.description: Where unknown local parts go. Null means they are refused during the SMTP session, which is the default and the safe one. A legacy domain's catch-all must be a confirmed destination; a BYO domain's is any address, because the mail lands on the customer's own server.

default_quota_bytes.description: BYO domains only: what a new mailbox here is given when no quota is named. 0 means none.

verified_at.description: Set the first time the MX is seen pointing at us (legacy) or at the server (BYO).

records.description: The records we publish for this domain (legacy) or expect and check (BYO), and why

MailDomainCreate.description: Either zone_id (legacy: a zone you host here) OR server_id + name (BYO: your own server, any domain).

zone_id.description: Legacy path: a zone you host here, already active

server_id.description: BYO path: an online mail server (srv_…)

name.description: BYO path: the domain name — need not be hosted on Orbit DNS

zone_name.description: Alias for `name` on the BYO path

catch_all.description: Legacy only; must be a confirmed destination

default_quota_bytes.description: BYO only. What a mailbox created on this domain gets when no quota is given; 0 means none.

backup_enabled.description: BYO only. Turning it on mints the domain's backup key; turning it off stops new backups (existing objects are not retroactively deleted).

checks.description: Ports, outbound 25, PTR, queue length, free disk — from the last report

install_cmd.description: Copy-paste onto the VPS as root

user_email.description: Who was given this mailbox at mail.yunzheng.space

user_bound.description: Whether that person has signed in yet, which is when their IdP subject is bound

send_limit_hour.description: Messages per clock hour; 0 means unmetered

last_activity_at.description: The later of the last message indexed into it and the last message it submitted

shared_with.description: YunZheng accounts that can also open this mailbox, read and send as it

collab.description: A collaborative inbox: conversations are assigned to one of the people with access and marked done

app_passwords.description: Never the hash or the plaintext — only what identifies each issued password

user_email.description: Who uses this mailbox at mail.yunzheng.space. Their IdP subject is bound on their first sign-in from this address; empty unassigns it.

send_limit_hour.description: Messages this mailbox may send in one clock hour. 0 means unmetered; the default is 200.

shared_with.description: The complete list of other YunZheng accounts (by email) that can open this mailbox; replaces the current list

collab.description: Work this mailbox as a collaborative inbox

members.description: Internal members ({mailbox_id}) each get their own copy; external members ({address}) are forwarded with SRS.

allow_external_senders.description: Off by default: an open group address is a spam relay with a friendly name.

members_can_send.description: Internal members may send as the group's address; each gets a confirmed sending identity for it

MailBoxImport.description: Either `rows` or `csv` (local,display,quota_bytes — a header line is ignored).

password.description: Shown once. Use it for 587/465 SMTP AUTH.

raw_url.description: Short-lived signed link straight to the node (5 minutes)

local_part.description: The part before the @, or * for a catch-all

MailLogEntry.description: The envelope and the verdict. Subjects and bodies are never recorded.

next_offset.description: Offset of the next page, or null when this is the last one

block_mode.description: What a blocked name is answered with: `nxdomain` (the name does not exist), `zero` (0.0.0.0 / ::), or `page` (the resolver's own address, which serves a notice over HTTP)

filter_lists.description: Comma-separated subscribed blocklists: `l2` (ads, trackers, malware — standard), `l3` (the same, strict), `nsfw` (adult content). Merged; the allowlist overrides all of them

rules.description: AdBlock DNS syntax, one rule per line

schedule_json.description: When blocking is PAUSED, per service id

tz.description: IANA time-zone name used by the schedules

safesearch.description: google, youtube, bing, duckduckgo, yandex, pixabay

block_bypass.description: Answer the probes clients use to route around this resolver

log_mode.description: Always `off` on a resolver with no owner

ratelimit.description: Queries per second per client, counted per PoP

paused_until.description: RFC3339; filtering is suspended until then

rules.description: Rules to test instead of the saved ones

client_id.description: 6-32 of a-z 0-9 -; carried in the DoH path and the TLS name

revoke.description: Revoke the existing token instead of issuing one

token.description: Shown once; only its hash is stored

url.description: Call this from the router on a schedule

delegation.description: Daily re-check of the public NS delegation for active zones

lost_at.description: Set while the public DNS tree reports name servers other than ns1/ns2.yunzheng.space; the zone keeps being served

secondary_master.description: Master IP when served as a secondary zone

mode.description: host: the apex is a single hostname, delegated with NS records inside the customer's existing zone

secondary_master.description: Set an IP to serve as secondary; null/empty to go back to primary

to.description: "me" or "team:<id>" — you must be owner/admin on both sides

tsig.description: true = generate a TSIG key (once); false = remove it

text.description: Zone file in BIND master format (what most DNS providers export): $ORIGIN / $TTL, relative and absolute names, @, parenthesised multi-line records, quoted TXT strings, ; comments. Up to 200000 characters.

mode.description: preview: parse and compare with the zone's records, write nothing; apply: write

replace.description: apply only: replace existing records that share a name and type with an imported one (otherwise the imported record is added next to them). Exact duplicates are always skipped.

status.description: duplicate: identical record exists; conflict: a record with the same name and type but other content exists

existing.description: conflict only: contents of the existing records

proxied_hint.description: The source marked this record as proxied; not applied

replaced.description: apply only: existing records removed by replace

error_hint.description: preview only: why apply would be refused (record limit)

cache_mode.description: Without origin directives: all = every cacheable response incl. HTML, static = static content types only, origin = only explicit max-age

cache_html_ttl.description: mode all: TTL for text/html without origin directives (0 = cache_ttl)

sense.description: Presence sensor. The per-site signing key is never returned.

dns_mode.description: zone: a proxied record in a hosted zone; cname: the customer's DNS CNAMEs to Orbit's target zone

Waf.description: The web application firewall for this site. The rule set is the OWASP Core Rule Set, scored: every rule that matches adds to an anomaly score, and the request is refused once the score reaches the threshold.

mode.description: monitor records what would have been refused, without refusing it

paranoia.description: How much the rule set looks for. Higher levels catch more and also flag more ordinary requests

threshold.description: Anomaly score at which a request is refused; one critical finding scores 5

exclusions.description: Rules that do not apply under a path

body.description: Inspect request bodies as well as the URL and the headers

legacy.description: Also apply the older pattern rules, before the rule set

rule.description: Rule id, as shown in the rule hits table

path_prefix.description: The rule is skipped for request paths starting with this

WafPatch.description: Every field is optional; only the ones present change.

WafHits.description: Which firewall rules have been matching, folded from the sampled request logs.

sampled.description: Always true: counts come from the sample, not from every request

example_path.description: One path the rule matched on, query string removed

origin_host_header.description: Reach a hostname origin by its own name: Host and SNI are the origin hostname and the visitor's host is sent in X-Forwarded-Host. For origins that route by Host.

service_id.description: Owning DNS service; defaults to the account's first

Instructions.description: What to add at the customer's DNS provider

cname.description: CNAME target seen in public DNS

oneOf.description: Accepted for compatibility: true sets mode to block, false sets it to off

sense.description: Presence sensor: off (nothing injected), observe (scored and logged only) or enforce (a navigation scoring below the threshold, or none at all from an address taking several pages a minute, meets the browser check).

urls.description: Paths to purge; omit to purge everything

purged.description: URLs purged, or 0 for a full purge

zone_id.description: Use instead of site_id for a zone-wide rule

roas.description: Included when listing CAs, so a client need not fetch each CA's ROAs separately

xml.description: RFC 8183 parent response from your RIR portal

principal.description: Who the token acts as: your email, or team:<id> for a team token

platform_mntner.description: Add this to your inet(6)num mnt-domains for the credential-free path

mntner.description: Maintainer the key is authorised for

cidrs.description: The block in CIDR form (RIPE keys IPv4 blocks as ranges)

covers.description: More-specific blocks of this allocation that RIPE also returns; they are folded into this row because they resolve to the same reverse zones

LogEntry.description: One request handled by the Orbit edge, identified by its Ray ID. Records are a sample: every security event is kept; pass-through requests are capped at about 200 per minute per site per point of presence.

action.description: waf-unavailable: the request was served without being inspected, because the rule engine did not answer

waf.description: What the firewall made of this request; null when the site has no firewall, or the request was not inspected

sense.description: Presence sensor score this request carried; null when it carried none

LogDetail.description: LogEntry plus every request header and connection detail

ja4.description: JA4 fingerprint of the TLS handshake: what the client's TLS library looks like, which no header can change. Null for plain HTTP.

h2fp.description: HTTP/2 fingerprint: the connection's opening settings, window update, priority and pseudo-header order. Null on HTTP/1.1.

pop_city.description: City of the point of presence that served the request

headers.description: Request headers as received; cookie / authorization values are redacted at the edge. `_truncated: true` marks a header set cut at 4 KB.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next (older) page; null on the last page

sampled.description: Always true: logs are a sample, counters in /analytics are exact

totals.description: Exact counters from the per-minute statistics

waf_block.description: Requests the firewall refused; a subset of blocked

waf_monitor.description: Requests the firewall would have refused in block mode; these were served

sense.description: Presence sensor. The share and the average come from the sampled rows; the two counts are exact.

csp_blocked.description: Origin fills where the site's own Content-Security-Policy refused the script

series.description: One point per bucket, oldest first, zero-filled

sampled_sections.description: Which sections derive from the sample rather than exact counters

VerifySite.description: A Verify site key. The server secret is returned only by create and rotate.

hostnames.description: Allowed page hostnames; empty = any. `*.example.com` matches every name under example.com

mode.description: managed: invisible, escalates to a checkbox when in doubt; invisible: never shows a checkbox; interactive: always asks for the click

fingerprint.description: Opt-in device digest (canvas / WebGL / audio / fonts hashed in the browser, salted per key). Default false

interaction.description: How hard this key insists a human was on the page. off: one signal among many. soft: no interaction costs score. strict: no interaction always asks for the checkbox. present: strict, and the page must have been visible and focused throughout. No level ever refuses a visitor outright — the worst any of them does is ask for a click, which a keyboard reaches with Tab and Space.

hostnames.description: Allowed hostnames (or a comma-separated string). Empty = any

VerifyInsights.description: Aggregates over the key's verification events (30-day retention); never individual rows

distinct_devices.description: Distinct device digests (only when fingerprint is on)

VerifySiteCreated.description: VerifySite plus the secret, shown once

secret.description: Server secret for /v1/siteverify (ovs_…) — store it now, it is never shown again

series.description: One point per bucket, oldest first, zero-filled

month.description: Metering: siteverify calls this calendar month across the account, and the pack limit (0 = unmetered)

BillingStatus.description: The account's Stripe subscription and the packs on sale. Every other billing route answers 503 billing_not_configured while Stripe is not set up on the platform; this one answers with configured=false instead.

configured.description: Stripe is set up on the platform

customer.description: A Stripe customer exists for this account

status.description: Stripe subscription status (active, trialing, past_due, canceled, …)

plans.description: Pack ids the subscription's prices map to

live.description: The packs are currently applied (active, trialing or past_due)

addon.description: Layered on top of the subscription pack (a paid Verify pack) rather than replacing it

url.description: Stripe Checkout URL to send the browser to; null when the running subscription was changed in place

updated.description: true: the existing subscription was changed (upgrade/downgrade or add-on added); the packs follow once Stripe confirms

url.description: Stripe Customer Portal URL (payment method, cancel, invoices)
